about: Flocking birds for the herd aggregation rule (pipeline/herds.py flocks): which birds gather in flocks, where (guild), how big a flock typically is by season, and which fly in V or echelon skeins. Matched by genus first, then family. A recorded per-group fine-tune: the typical flock sizes are modelling values read from the sources named, not counts. Seasons are the northern hemisphere's (swapped on a southern tile).

guilds.grazer: open grass and wet meadow near water, low ground (geese, cranes)
guilds.field: open fields and grass, a little drawn to water (blackbirds, starlings)

geese.source: Bellrose, F. C. (1980). Ducks, Geese and Swans of North America. Stackpole (family groups merging into wintering flocks of tens to hundreds); Raveling, D. G. (1969). Social classes of Canada geese in winter. Journal of Wildlife Management 33: 304-318

cranes.source: Tacha, T. C., Nesbitt, S. A. and Vohs, P. A. (1992). Sandhill Crane. The Birds of North America 31 (pairs and family groups in summer; staging and wintering flocks of hundreds to thousands)

ducks.source: Bellrose, F. C. (1980). Ducks, Geese and Swans of North America. Stackpole (wintering rafts of tens; pairs and broods in summer; echelons and loose V's in flight)

coots.source: Alisauskas, R. T. and Arnold, T. W. (1994). American Coot. In: Migratory Shore and Upland Game Bird Management in North America (wintering rafts of tens to hundreds)

pelicans.source: Knopf, F. L. and Evans, R. M. (2004). American White Pelican. The Birds of North America 57 (cooperative foraging flocks; lines and V's in flight)

blackbirds.source: Orians, G. H. (1985). Blackbirds of the Americas. University of Washington Press (mixed winter flocks of hundreds to thousands on fields)

starlings.source: Feare, C. (1984). The Starling. Oxford University Press (feeding flocks of hundreds outside the breeding season)

skeins.about: Migration skeins over a tile in spring (north) and fall (south): per V-flying migratory species, skeins per hour = base x migration (AVONET Migration: 3 migratory 1.0, 2 partial 0.4, 1 sedentary none) x the season's passage (its share of the year's open-licence GBIF records over a quarter, 0.3-3). Height and speed are drawn per skein within the ranges. The heading follows the tile's valley axis toward north in spring and south in fall, half pulled to true north-south.
skeins.source: Hummel, D. (1983). Aerodynamic aspects of formation flight in birds. Journal of Theoretical Biology 104: 321-347; Portugal, S. J. et al. (2014). Upwash exploitation and downwash avoidance by flap phasing in ibis formation flight. Nature 505: 399-402 (the lead changes, the phase along the arms); Gauthreaux, S. A. (1991) for migration heights
